pages.html:
A 100-patient single-centre blinded RCT found similar response (96% vs 88%) with quetiapine 25–50 mg vs haloperidol 1–2 mg/day; shorter ICU stay and more sleep with quetiapine were soft secondaries. No placebo arm, tiny haloperidol dose. Keep haloperidol first (AID-ICU), use quetiapine for parkinsonism or EPS risk.

pages.html:
p=0.052 for death; more pneumonia with ICS (TORCH).

pages.title: ICU fluids — the summary
pages.html:
Colloids, albumin and HES: no mortality benefit, HES harmful. Balanced crystalloids reduce MAKE30 (SMART) though PLUS was neutral. Restrictive vs liberal strategy after resuscitation: no mortality difference (CLASSIC, CLOVERS, ARISE FLUIDS).

pages.title: ICU glucose target 6–10 mmol/L, not 'normal'
pages.html:
Tight control (4.5–6) increased 90-day mortality and hypoglycaemia (NICE-SUGAR).

pages.title: ICU glucose target stays <10 mmol/L, even with a hypoglycaemia-safe tight protocol
pages.html:
TGC-Fast (n=9230, no early PN): computer-guided 4.4–6.1 mmol/L control achieved low severe-hypoglycaemia rates (1.0% vs 0.7%) yet made no difference to ICU LOS (HR 1.00) or 90-day mortality (10.5% vs 10.1%). Secondary renal signals are hypothesis-generating. NICE-SUGAR's harm was likely hypoglycaemia plus early PN, but removing those still shows no benefit — so avoid early PN, target 6–10 mmol/L and never hypoglycaemia.

Trial: TGC-Fast

Source: The Bottom Line — TGC-Fast review

pages.title: Start naltrexone at hospital discharge for AUD — oral or injectable both work
pages.html:
No difference in heavy drinking days; injectable improves adherence but costs ~3× more. Choose on preference and access (ADOPT).

Source: ADOPT

pages.title: In septic ventilated patients, dexmedetomidine and propofol are equivalent
pages.html:
Same delirium-free days, mortality and cognition (MENDS2) — choose on haemodynamics and cost.

Trial: MENDS2

Source: MENDS2

pages.title: In stable CAD, revascularise for symptoms, not prognosis
pages.html:
Even with moderate–severe ischaemia, an initial invasive strategy didn't cut CV events (ISCHEMIA). Optimise medical therapy first.

Trial: ISCHEMIA

pages.title: Intensive HbA1c (≤6.5%) in T2DM reduces nephropathy, not death
pages.html:
Gliclazide-based control; no excess mortality (ADVANCE).

pages.title: Intermediate-high-risk PE with RV strain: don't reflexively fill — a 40 mg furosemide bolus is safe
pages.html:
Ferrari (n=60): furosemide vs 1.5 L saline gave the same troponin kinetics; diuretic lowered BNP, sPAP and IVC faster with no harm. If IVC is plethoric and RV dilated, offloading is reasonable; reserve cautious fluid for a low CVP.

Trial: Ferrari (PE diuretics)

Source: The Bottom Line — Ferrari review

pages.title: Intubated for acute brain injury? Give one dose of ceftriaxone 2 g to prevent early VAP
pages.html:
PROPHY-VAP (blinded, n=319): single 2 g IV ceftriaxone within 12 h of intubation in TBI/stroke/SAH with GCS ≤12 halved early VAP (14% vs 32%, HR 0.60), with more ventilator-free (9 vs 5) and antibiotic-free (21 vs 15) days and lower 28-day mortality (15% vs 25%), no resistance or C. difficile signal. Consistent with SDD data; TBL calls it practice-changing. Not tested in cardiac arrest, tumour or infective coma, or with subglottic-drainage tubes.

Trial: PROPHY-VAP

Source: The Bottom Line — PROPHY-VAP review

pages.title: IV amino acids cut creatinine-defined AKI after cardiac bypass surgery, but not RRT or long-term renal function
pages.html:
2 g/kg/day amino acids from theatre for up to 72 h: KDIGO AKI 26.9% vs 31.7% (RR 0.85, NNT 21), stage 3 AKI halved, RRT 1.4% vs 1.9% (NS), creatinine identical at 30–180 d. Biochemical benefit only — not yet a reason to change practice.

Trial: PROTECTION

Source: The Bottom Line — PROTECTION review

pages.title: A KDIGO supportive-care bundle cuts moderate/severe post-op AKI — but not RRT or death
pages.html:
BigpAK-2: in biomarker-positive high-risk surgical patients, PLR-guided fluid, MAP >65, CI >2.5, holding ACEi/ARB 48 h and nephrotoxins 72 h, and glucose 5.5–8.3 reduced KDIGO 2–3 AKI at 72 h from 22% to 14% (OR 0.57). Any-AKI, RRT, 90-day mortality and MAKE90 unchanged — the bundle downgrades AKI severity rather than preventing it.

Trial: BigpAK-2

Source: The Bottom Line — BigpAK-2 review

pages.title: Start carvedilol in cirrhosis with new ascites even without high-risk varices
pages.html:
Halved ascites complications and AKI, fewer paracenteses, borderline lower mortality (CARVE-AS, n=104). Treats portal hypertension, not just varices; stop for refractory ascites with hypotension/AKI.

Trial: CARVE-AS

Source: CARVE-AS

pages.title: Ketamine for RSI in the shocked patient: dose by ideal body weight and consider ≤1 mg/kg
pages.html:
RSI trial critique: ketamine was dosed by actual body weight (median 1.6 mg/kg, a quarter received >2 mg/kg) in a population where half were overweight — likely contributing to more post-induction hypotension (SBP drop >30 mmHg 24% vs 15% with etomidate). Lower doses (0.5–1 mg/kg IBW) in sepsis/APACHE ≥20 were not tested; mortality was identical either way.

Trial: RSI trial (Casey et al.)

Source: The Bottom Line — RSI trial review

pages.title: Lenient rate control (<110 at rest) is fine in permanent AF
pages.html:

Better 18-month survival in an open-label Italian trial (ANSWER); not replicated by PRECIOSA.

pages.html:
No change in wean time, ICU stay or readmission (MIDAS).

No outcome difference (DoReMi) — choose on BP, renal function and availability.

pages.title: Don't β-block tachycardia in septic shock on noradrenaline
pages.html:
STRESS-L: landiolol titrated to HR 80–94 did not improve SOFA, raised noradrenaline requirement, quadrupled serious adverse events (25% vs 6%) and trended to higher 28/90-day mortality; stopped early. pages.title: No empiric cryoprecipitate in trauma haemorrhage — guide fibrinogen by ROTEM/Clauss
pages.html:

Give fibrinogen when it is measured low (FIBTEM A5 or Clauss <1.5–2 g/L), not blind to all bleeders.

pages.html:

Less haematoma growth and fewer early deaths but no functional benefit at 90 days (TICH-2).

pages.title: Non-STEMI OHCA: nearest ED is fine — no routine bypass to a cardiac arrest centre
pages.html:

Pairs with COACT/TOMAHAWK: in non-STEMI OHCA, prioritise ICU stabilisation and neuroprotection over early cath lab. Possible benefit under ~57 y is hypothesis-generating.

pages.title: Obese patient after extubation: prophylactic NIV for 48 h is reasonable, though unproven over HFNC
pages.html:

Cost: more intolerance (15% vs 4%) and longer ICU stay. Use NIV in obese patients with extra risk factors; HFNC is acceptable if NIV not tolerated.

pages.title: OVISS is reinforcement learning on retrospective data, not an RCT — hypothesis, not mandate
pages.html:
The 'start vasopressin at NA ~0.2 mcg/kg/min, SOFA ~7, lactate ~2.5, ~4 h from shock onset' policy came from a model trained on 3608 and validated on 10,845 EHR patients; concordance with the model was associated with lower mortality (aOR 0.81) and less RRT (aOR 0.47). E-value only 1.46; needs prospective trial. Earlier vasopressin is reasonable and cheap, but the evidence base is observational.

Source: The Bottom Line — OVISS review

pages.title: Pancreatitis fluids: 10 mL/kg LR bolus only if hypovolaemic, then 1.5 mL/kg/h for ~20 h

pages.html:

pages.title: Refractory VF after 3 shocks: switch to AP pads or double sequential defibrillation
pages.html:
DOSE VF (cluster-crossover, n=405): survival to discharge 30.4% with DSED and 21.7% with vector change vs 13.3% standard anterior-lateral shocks; DSED also improved ROSC (46% vs 27%) and mRS ≤2 (27% vs 11%). Stopped early, few events, as-treated analysis NS — so not definitive, but changing pad vector (or DSED with a second defibrillator, shocks <1 s apart) is a reasonable move once VF has survived three standard shocks and an antiarrhythmic.

Trial: DOSE VF

Source: The Bottom Line — DOSE VF review

pages.title: Refractory VF: consider ECPR where available
pages.html:
43% vs 7% neuro-intact survival in a single-centre trial (ARREST) — needs a system, not just a device.

Trial: ARREST

Source: ARREST

pages.title: Restrictive transfusion (Hb 70) is safe in stable ICU patients
pages.html:
Lower 30-day mortality in younger/less sick patients; except active ACS (TRICC).

Trial: TRICC

Source: TRICC

pages.title: After the first litre in septic shock, early pressors with less fluid is as good as more fluid — not better
pages.html:
ARISE FLUIDS (2026): same days alive out of hospital at 90 days, less pulmonary oedema, more ICU admissions. Third neutral trial after CLASSIC and CLOVERS — pick the strategy that fits the patient.

Trial: ARISE FLUIDS

Source: ARISE FLUIDS

pages.title: Ringer's lactate is safe in renal patients — saline causes more hyperkalaemia
pages.html:
Saline worsened potassium and acidosis in kidney transplantation (O'Malley 2005); don't avoid LR for the potassium.

Trial: O'Malley et al.

Source: O'Malley et al.

pages.title: Rivaroxaban is non-inferior to warfarin in higher-risk AF
pages.html:
Similar stroke/embolism; less ICH but more GI bleeding (ROCKET-AF).

Trial: ROCKET-AF

Source: ROCKET-AF

pages.title: Rivers taught us early recognition and treatment matters — the protocol didn't
pages.html:
Single-centre 2001 trial, superseded by ProCESS/ARISE/ProMISe; keep the urgency, drop the ScvO2 targets.

Trial: Rivers EGDT

Source: Rivers EGDT

pages.title: Routine 7-day hydrocortisone in severe CAP may harm
pages.html:
90-day mortality 15% vs 9.8% (OR 1.56), imbalanced randomisation; influenza strata too small to judge (REMAP-CAP).

Trial: REMAP-CAP (corticosteroid domain)

Source: REMAP-CAP (corticosteroid domain)

pages.title: Routine IV paracetamol in sepsis doesn't improve organ-support-free days
pages.html:
1 g IV 6-hourly for 5 days vs placebo: 20.2 vs 19.6 organ-support-free days (NS), safe (no hepatotoxicity/hypotension). Less ARDS (2.2% vs 8.5%) and a mortality trend were unadjusted secondaries only. Combined with HEAT, no indication for scheduled paracetamol as a sepsis therapy.

Trial: ASTER

Source: The Bottom Line — ASTER review

pages.title: Run ARDS dry once out of shock
pages.html:
Conservative fluids gave ~2.5 more ventilator-free days and shorter ICU stay, no mortality cost (FACTT).

Trial: FACTT

Source: FACTT

pages.title: Sedate with propofol or dexmedetomidine, not benzodiazepines
pages.html:
Less delirium and shorter ventilation (PADIS 2018).

Trial: PADIS Guidelines

Source: PADIS Guidelines

pages.title: Seizing or comatose from hyponatraemia with no 3% on the ward: 2 ml/kg 8.4% bicarbonate now
pages.html:
≈ 4 ml/kg 3% saline; raises Na ~2–3 mmol/L (Gutierrez 1991, Kim 1996, Bourdeaux 2010). Less dire: 1.5 ml/kg ≈ 100 ml / two ampoules. Ideally central, peripheral in an emergency; avoid if significantly alkalotic.

Source: PulmCrit hyponatraemia series (Farkas) + SGEM/RebelEM/AJKD blog — screenshots 19/10/2026

pages.title: Sepsis Six isn't 'six things in an hour for everyone' any more
pages.html:
UK Sepsis Trust's revised bundle (2019): 1 senior clinician attends → 2 oxygen only if needed (94–98%, 88–92% if CO2-retainer) → 3 IV access, bloods incl. cultures + lactate → 4 IV antibiotics → 5 IV fluids (500 ml boluses, reassess; more on senior advice) → 6 monitor (NEWS2, urine output, repeat lactate). Then NICE NG51 (2024 update, after the Academy of Medical Royal Colleges 2022 statement on antibiotic timing) made it risk-stratified: screen with NEWS2, not qSOFA. High risk (NEWS2 ≥7, or 5–6 with a red flag such as lactate >2, mottling, new AKI, deterioration) = full bundle within 1 h, clock from the triggering obs. Moderate risk (NEWS2 5–6, or 1–4 with a flag) = senior review and investigations first, antibiotics within 3 h if still indicated. The point is fewer reflex broad-spectrum antibiotics in people who turn out not to have sepsis, without losing the hour in the ones who do.

Source: UK Sepsis Trust 2019 revision; NICE NG51 (2024); AoMRC 2022 — cross-checked against an NHS trust guideline v5 Oct 2025

pages.title: Septic or very sick patient needing RSI: ketamine carries more peri-intubation collapse than etomidate
pages.html:
NNH ~10 in sepsis/APACHE II ≥20 (RSI trial 2025). Consider etomidate, reduced-dose ketamine or pressors ready.

Trial: RSI trial (Casey et al.)

Source: RSI trial (Casey et al.)

pages.title: Sequential nephron blockade in acute HF — ESC 2026
pages.html:
IV acetazolamide or oral HCTZ as class IIa add-on to loop diuretic. HCTZ causes hypokalaemia and creatinine rise — check U&E daily. Acetazolamide may suit advanced CKD. Stay IV until decongested.

Source: ESC HF guideline 2026 (from your notes)

pages.title: Severe acidaemia (pH ≤7.20) with AKI stage 2–3: bicarbonate may reduce RRT and death
pages.html:
Overall neutral; AKI subgroup is the signal; watch sodium, calcium and alkalosis (BICAR-ICU 2018).

Trial: BICAR-ICU

Source: BICAR-ICU

pages.title: Severe CAP in ICU: hydrocortisone halves 28-day mortality
pages.html:
6% vs 12%, given early, 200 mg/day with taper (CAPE COD). REMAP-CAP's 7-day course didn't replicate — select carefully.

Trial: CAPE COD

Source: CAPE COD

pages.title: Severe hyponatraemia: slow correction (<8 mEq/L/24 h) is associated with worse survival

props.v: Mark et al (Kaiser) — hyponatraemia correction rate

pages.html:
Fast and medium correction had fewer deaths/neuro events; ODS rare at every rate — the 8 mEq/L ceiling is under review (Mark 2026).

Trial: Mark et al (Kaiser) — hyponatraemia correction rate

Source: Mark et al (Kaiser) — hyponatraemia correction rate

pages.title: Severe respiratory failure: refer to an ECMO centre
pages.html:
Referral improved survival without severe disability — the pathway, not just the pump (CESAR).

Trial: CESAR

Source: CESAR

pages.title: Severe stroke: don't rush the tracheostomy — waiting to day 10 lets a third avoid it
pages.html:
SETPOINT2: trach by day 5 vs from day 10 gave the same 6-month functional outcome and mortality; 33% of the standard-timing group were extubated or died before needing one. Early trach only adds a ~17–20% complication-rate procedure.

Trial: SETPOINT2

Source: The Bottom Line — SETPOINT2 review

pages.title: SGLT2 inhibitors help HFpEF/HFmrEF too
pages.html:
Dapagliflozin cut worsening HF/CV death across LVEF >40% (DELIVER).

Trial: DELIVER

Source: DELIVER

pages.title: SGLT2 inhibitors save lives in T2DM with CVD
pages.html:
CV death 3.7% vs 5.9% — the trial that changed diabetes care (EMPA-REG).

Trial: EMPA-REG

Source: EMPA-REG

pages.title: SODa-BIC: bicarbonate halves recurrent acidosis but not MAKE30 — watch the potassium
pages.html:
8.4% bicarbonate to pH 7.30–7.35 for 5 h in vasopressor-dependent patients with pH <7.30: MAKE30 40% vs 39% (placebo), RRT 17% vs 21% and RRT-dependence 6% vs 9% (NS), recurrence of acidosis 32% vs 56%, all adverse events were hypokalaemia <3.0. Use it for specific physiological goals (severe acidaemia, hyperkalaemia, deferring KRT), with potassium checks.

Trial: SODa-BIC

Source: The Bottom Line — SODa-BIC review

pages.title: Sodium overcorrection is usually the kidneys, not your infusion
pages.html:
Once the cause of ADH release is fixed (volume, nausea, drug), vasopressin switches off and the kidneys dump free water — the sodium climbs regardless of what you're giving. Anticipate it in any reversible cause (hypovolaemia, polydipsia, drugs).

Source: PulmCrit hyponatraemia series (Farkas) + SGEM/RebelEM/AJKD blog — screenshots 19/10/2026

pages.title: Spironolactone cuts mortality in severe HFrEF
pages.html:
~30% relative reduction in death; watch potassium and creatinine (RALES).

Trial: RALES

Source: RALES

pages.title: Conservative SpO2 90% (88–92%) target in ventilated ICU patients doesn't improve survival
pages.html:
UK-ROX (n=16,500): 90-day mortality 35.4% vs 34.9% with usual care; no subgroup (sepsis, HIE, brain injury) benefited. Avoid hyperoxia on physiological grounds, but there's no mortality case for driving SpO2 down to 90%; a usual 92–96% target is fine.

Trial: UK-ROX

Source: The Bottom Line — UK-ROX review

pages.title: Surviving Sepsis 2026: what actually changed from 2021
pages.html:
Prescott et al, Crit Care Med 2026 — 129 recommendations, only 17 strong. Screening: formal move away from qSOFA; MEWS-type scores (≥4 urgent review), and screen pre-hospital. Fluids: 30 ml/kg kept but 'revisited' — conditional, individualise, reassess often, use adjusted body weight if BMI >30; balanced crystalloids over saline; against upfront albumin; new conditional support for active de-resuscitation once stable. Pressors: bolus then noradrenaline if still hypotensive, concurrent in unstable shock; peripheral noradrenaline endorsed (low dose, big proximal cannula); non-invasive BP acceptable in selected patients. MAP ~65, 60–65 acceptable ≥65 years. Antibiotics: immediate for probable/definite sepsis or shock, risk-stratified deferral when sepsis unlikely and no shock; prolonged/continuous beta-lactam infusion after a loading dose now STRONG; de-escalation now strong; PCT to stop, not to start; against empirical antifungals or anaerobic cover without risk factors; new conditional for SDD in ventilated patients where resistance is low. Steroids: hydrocortisone conditional in shock on pressors (immune dysregulation framing). Against: beta-blockers, vitamin C, IVIG, haemoperfusion, vitamin D, probiotics, bicarbonate for haemodynamics. Awake proning conditional.

Source: SSC 2026 (Prescott, CCM 2026) via Critical Care Update and Critical Care Commute summaries — verify against the full guideline

pages.title: Stable AKI-D on IHD: dialyse to indication, not to a Mon/Wed/Fri schedule
pages.html:
LIBERATE-D (JAMA 2026): triggers of urea >~40 mmol/L, K >6 (or >5.5 despite treatment), pH <7.15, or volume-overload hypoxaemia after diuretics cut sessions from 3.1 to 1.8/week, gave 21 vs 5 dialysis-free days by day 28 and recovery in 2 vs 8.5 days, with no excess harm (recovery-by-discharge benefit lost significance after adjustment). Applies once off pressors/ventilation — not to CRRT decisions in the unstable patient.

Trial: LIBERATE-D

Source: The Bottom Line — LIBERATE-D review

pages.title: Stable CAD on anticoagulation: stop the aspirin
pages.html:
Adding aspirin to OAC in stented, high-risk stable CAD increased CV events (16.9% vs 12.1%), tripled major bleeding and raised death; stopped early (AQUATIC).

Trial: AQUATIC

Source: AQUATIC

pages.title: Start an SGLT2 inhibitor in HFrEF regardless of diabetes
pages.html:
Dapagliflozin cut CV death/worsening HF by ~26% on top of standard therapy (DAPA-HF).

Trial: DAPA-HF

Source: DAPA-HF

pages.title: Start vasopressin earlier — around noradrenaline 0.2 mcg/kg/min
pages.html:
Earlier initiation associated with lower mortality (OVISS, OR 0.81); observational/RL analysis.

Trial: OVISS

Source: OVISS

pages.title: Steroids don't prevent septic shock — use them once shock is established
pages.html:
No reduction in progression to shock in severe sepsis without shock (HYPRESS).

Trial: HYPRESS

Source: HYPRESS

pages.title: Steroids in ARDS: conditionally recommended if early, harmful if late
pages.html:
Dexamethasone 20 mg/d ×5 then 10 mg/d ×5 within 24–72 h (generally <7 days). Starting >14 days after onset may be harmful.

Source: Daoud et al review 2026 (from your notes)

pages.title: Give steroids in hospitalised CAP when CRP >204 mg/L
pages.html:
Mortality 6.1% vs 13.0% above that threshold (OR 0.43); no benefit below it. Expect hyperglycaemia and more readmissions (Smit IPD meta-analysis 2025).

Trial: Trial name to confirm

Source: Trial name to confirm

pages.title: Steroids in septic shock: the pendulum summary
pages.html:
Mortality results alternate across Annane, CORTICUS, ADRENAL, APROCCHSS; faster shock reversal is the one consistent finding. SSC 2026 / SCCM 2024: conditional suggestion for hydrocortisone 200 mg/day in shock needing ongoing pressors, low certainty.

Source: SSC 2026 / SCCM 2024 (from your notes)

pages.title: Stop antibiotics ~4 days after source control
pages.html:
Fixed short course non-inferior to longer therapy in intra-abdominal infection (STOP-IT).

Trial: STOP-IT

Source: STOP-IT

pages.title: A subcutaneous furosemide pump can get congested HF patients home ~5 days earlier
pages.html:
+4 days alive and out of hospital at 30 days, SAEs no different (SUBCUT-HF II, 20 UK sites). Needs home review every 3 days and a readmission signal (14% vs 6%) to keep an eye on.

Trial: SUBCUT-HF II

Source: SUBCUT-HF II

pages.title: Supraglottic airway is acceptable in out-of-hospital arrest
pages.html:
No ROSC difference vs intubation (SAVE); prioritise compressions.

Trial: SAVE

Source: SAVE

pages.title: Switch stable HFrEF from ACE-i to sacubitril/valsartan
pages.html:
20% fewer CV deaths/HF admissions vs enalapril; 36-h ACE-i washout to avoid angioedema (PARADIGM-HF).

Trial: PARADIGM-HF

Source: PARADIGM-HF

pages.title: Target a 5 mmol/L rise for symptoms, then ≤6 mmol/L per 24 h on average
pages.html:
ODS risk tracks the average rate over a day, not minute-to-minute swings — so aggressive small boluses to hit a slow curve are safer than drifting. 10/24 h and 18/48 h are thresholds for harm, not goals (Sterns).

Source: PulmCrit hyponatraemia series (Farkas) + SGEM/RebelEM/AJKD blog — screenshots 19/10/2026

pages.title: TBI: TXA within 3 h is reasonable in mild–moderate head injury, not severe
pages.html:
Neutral overall; head-injury death reduced only in GCS 9–15 given early (CRASH-3).

Trial: CRASH-3

Source: CRASH-3

pages.title: The DDAVP clamp: 2 mcg IV 8-hourly + free water <1 L/day, no hypotonic IV fluids
pages.html:
Blocks renal water excretion so sodium only moves with what you infuse — Adrogué-Madias then actually works. Candidates: reversible cause of hyponatraemia, especially chronic hyponatraemia, cirrhosis, alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalaemia or Na <120.

Source: PulmCrit hyponatraemia series (Farkas) + SGEM/RebelEM/AJKD blog — screenshots 19/10/2026

pages.title: Three ways to use DDAVP: rescue, reactive, proactive
pages.html:
Rescue — already overcorrected: DDAVP + D5W to bring Na back down. Reactive — rising too fast: DDAVP + stop fluids to freeze it. Proactive — high ODS risk: DDAVP from the start with hypertonic saline so you control the whole curve.

Source: PulmCrit hyponatraemia series (Farkas) + SGEM/RebelEM/AJKD blog — screenshots 19/10/2026

pages.title: Ticagrelor over clopidogrel in ACS
pages.html:
Fewer CV deaths/MI/strokes without more overall major bleeding; expect dyspnoea (PLATO).

Trial: PLATO

Source: PLATO

pages.title: Tiotropium improves symptoms and exacerbations in COPD
pages.html:
No change in FEV1 decline, but fewer exacerbations and better QoL (UPLIFT).

Trial: UPLIFT

Source: UPLIFT

pages.title: Transfuse UGIB at Hb <70, not <90
pages.html:
Restrictive strategy lowered 45-day mortality and rebleeding; exclude exsanguination and ACS (Villanueva).

Trial: Villanueva

Source: Villanueva

pages.title: Trauma patients don't need 15 L/min — target SpO2 94–98%
pages.html:
Restrictive (SpO2 94%) vs liberal (15 L or FiO2 1.0) oxygen for the first 8 h after major trauma: death/major respiratory complication 16.1% vs 16.7% (OR 1.01). Neither harm nor benefit from restricting oxygen; ATLS-style routine high-flow oxygen is unnecessary in non-hypoxic patients.

Trial: TRAUMOX2

Source: The Bottom Line — TRAUMOX2 review

pages.title: Treat hypertension in the over-80s
pages.html:
Indapamide ± perindopril cut stroke, heart failure and all-cause death — age alone is not a reason to withhold treatment (HYVET).

Trial: HYVET

Source: HYVET

pages.title: Triple therapy in symptomatic COPD with exacerbations
pages.html:
Fewer moderate/severe exacerbations than either dual combination (IMPACT).

Trial: IMPACT

Source: IMPACT

pages.title: TXA benefit falls ~10% for every 15 minutes of delay — none after 3 hours
pages.html:
Start the clock at injury or birth; 3 h is a ceiling, not a target (CRASH-2/WOMAN pooled analysis).

pages.title: TXA in cardiac surgery: use the lower dose
pages.html:
Less bleeding and reoperation; seizures 0.7% vs 0.1% with high doses (ATACAS).

Source: ATACAS

pages.title: TXA in PPH — WHO/FIGO 2025 vs ACOG
pages.html:
WHO/FIGO: TXA within 3 h of PPH diagnosis, first-line with uterotonics and massage (MOTIVE bundle). ACOG: only if initial medical therapy fails. TXA is not a uterotonic.

pages.html:
CRASH-2 and PATCH reduced early deaths; STAAMP neutral. European 2023 guideline: TXA within 3 h; EAST 2025: conditional recommendation, no dose advice. No vascular occlusive signal.

Source: European trauma guideline 2023 / EAST 2025 (from your notes)

pages.title: TXA is routine in hip and knee arthroplasty
pages.html:
Less transfusion, no excess VTE (TRACTION).

Trial: TRACTION

Source: TRACTION

pages.title: Uncomplicated bacteraemia: 7 days of antibiotics is enough
pages.html:
BALANCE (n=3631): 7 vs 14 days non-inferior for 90-day mortality (−1.6%, CI −4.0 to 0.8), with 5 more antibiotic-free days and a day less in hospital; no excess relapse. Does not apply to S. aureus, endocarditis, osteomyelitis, undrained collections, prosthetic valves or profound immunosuppression — count from source control/first adequate dose.

Trial: BALANCE

pages.title: Use capillary refill time, not just lactate, to guide resuscitation
pages.html:
CRT-guided strategy: less fluid, off pressors sooner, win-ratio advantage; informs SSC 2026 (ANDROMEDA-SHOCK 2).

pages.html:
Higher first-pass success than palpation in meta-analyses; figures to confirm.

pages.title: Vaptans are the opposite of DDAVP — avoid them in hyponatraemia
pages.html:
They force an uncontrolled water diuresis and can overshoot into hypernatraemia and ODS (Malhotra 2014). European 2014 guideline recommends against; the supportive NEJM review relied on a manufacturer-funded panel.

Source: PulmCrit hyponatraemia series (Farkas) + SGEM/RebelEM/AJKD blog — screenshots 19/10/2026

pages.title: Vasopressin is a safe second pressor, not a mortality drug
pages.html:
No 28-day mortality benefit vs noradrenaline alone (VASST); possible benefit in less severe shock.

Trial: VASST

Source: VASST

pages.title: Ventilate ARDS at 6 ml/kg predicted body weight, Pplat <30
pages.html:
Low tidal volume cut mortality ~9% absolute (ARMA) — the core of lung-protective ventilation.

Trial: ARMA (ARDSNet)

Source: ARMA (ARDSNet)

pages.title: Ventilated patients: any SpO2 target from 90% to 98% is fine — aim ~94%
pages.html:
PILOT (n=2541): 90%, 94% and 98% targets gave identical ventilator-free days and mortality. Avoid frank hyperoxia, but don't chase a low target aggressively either; 92–96% is a sensible default.

Trial: PILOT

Source: The Bottom Line — PILOT review

pages.title: Ventilated patients get IV pantoprazole 40 mg daily — even when enterally fed
pages.html:
Pantoprazole vs placebo in 4821 ventilated adults: clinically important upper GI bleeding 1.0% vs 3.5% (HR 0.30, NNT 40) with no difference in 90-d mortality (29.1% vs 30.9%), VAP or C. difficile. Resolves the SUP-ICU/PEPTIC harm worries; continue for the duration of ventilation.

Trial: REVISE

Source: The Bottom Line — REVISE review

pages.title: Make video laryngoscopy the default first-attempt device
pages.html:
Collaborative VLS (n=8429, theatre) and DEVICE (ED/ICU) both show fewer attempts and higher first-pass success with VL vs direct laryngoscopy (98% vs 92% first-pass; failure 0.3% vs 4%). Caveat: VLS used a hyperangulated GlideScope + stylet, so results may not transfer to standard-geometry blades.

Trial: Collaborative VLS

Source: The Bottom Line — Collaborative VLS review

pages.title: Waiting for RRT indications avoids dialysis in half of patients
pages.html:
Delayed strategy: same mortality, fewer catheter infections (AKIKI).

Trial: AKIKI

Source: AKIKI

pages.title: Wake them up, then let them breathe — every day
pages.html:
Pair the daily sedation hold with the SBT rather than running them separately: in the ABC trial (Girard 2008) SAT→SBT gave 3 more ventilator-free days and 1-year mortality 44% vs 58% (NNT ≈7). Expect a few more self-extubations, not more reintubations. This is the 'B' of the ABCDEF bundle.

Trial: ABC trial — Girard (Lancet 2008)

Source: ABC trial (Girard 2008)

pages.title: Ward-based intermittent NIV for mild ARF: softer endpoint improved, hard outcomes unchanged
pages.html:
2-h CPAP/NIV cycles every 8 h cut 'progression to severe ARF' (18.5% vs 28.3%, NNT 11) but intubation, ICU admission, LOS and mortality were identical. Endpoint was mostly subjective respiratory distress in an unblinded trial. Low-/high-flow oxygen stays first line for most mild ARF.

Trial: NAVIGATE

Source: The Bottom Line — NAVIGATE review

pages.title: What EGDT actually is (and why UK practice never adopted it)
pages.html:
Early Goal-Directed Therapy = Rivers' 2001 six-hour ED protocol for septic shock: central line in, then hit targets in sequence — CVP 8–12 mmHg with crystalloid boluses, MAP ≥65 with vasopressors, then ScvO2 ≥70% by transfusing to haematocrit ≥30% and, if still low, adding dobutamine. One single-centre US trial (N=263) showed 30.5% vs 46.5% mortality, so it became the backbone of the US Surviving Sepsis bundles. ProCESS, ARISE and ProMISe (2014–15) then showed the catheter-driven targets added nothing once antibiotics and fluids were given promptly. The UK largely skipped the protocol and kept the useful parts — Sepsis Six, early antibiotics, 30 ml/kg if hypotensive/lactate ≥4, noradrenaline to MAP 65, lactate and CRT to guide reassessment. So when US sources say 'EGDT', read it as 'resuscitate early and properly', not 'chase CVP and ScvO2'.

Trial: Rivers EGDT

Source: Rivers 2001; ProCESS / ARISE / ProMISe

pages.title: When not to clamp: uncontrolled drinking, or pure hypervolaemic hyponatraemia
pages.html:
Psychogenic polydipsia + DDAVP = worse hyponatraemia. HF/cirrhosis patients rarely overcorrect and hypertonic saline worsens overload — unless hyponatraemia is multifactorial (then DDAVP + furosemide can work). SIADH of any cause: DDAVP is fine.

Source: PulmCrit hyponatraemia series (Farkas) + SGEM/RebelEM/AJKD blog — screenshots 19/10/2026

pages.title: Procedural MI (within 30 days)
pages.html:
Needs angiographic confirmation or other new imaging finding suggesting MI — troponin alone is not enough.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Pseudo-IBD: Behçet's with GI involvement
pages.html:
Intestinal Behçet's mimics Crohn's — oral/genital ulcers and uveitis point the other way.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Pseudogout involves more joints than gout
pages.html:
Polyarticular pattern favours CPPD over gout.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Pyogenic vs granulomatous osteomyelitis on biopsy
pages.html:
Granulomatous osteomyelitis (TB, fungal) shows absent neutrophils.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: ARDS lung-protective ventilation: "6 – 30 – 88/95 – 35"
pages.html:
VT 6 mL/kg PBW (start ~8 then reduce; PBW not actual weight), Pplat ≤30 cmH2O, SpO2 88–95%, RR up to 35/min for respiratory acidosis. Initial PEEP 5–8 cmH2O. Expiratory flow not reaching zero = auto-PEEP, so lengthen expiratory time (higher inspiratory flow shortens inspiratory time). Minute ventilation = VT × RR.

Source: Screenshot

pages.title: Hydrocortisone in septic shock restores pressor response: shortens vasopressor time, but doesn't reliably improve survival
pages.html:
Cortisol response is often inadequate in septic shock, so vessels ignore norepinephrine. Hydrocortisone restores adrenergic receptor response, reduces NO vasodilation and dampens cytokines. Dose: IV 200 mg/day as bolus or infusion; fludrocortisone 50 µg/day enteral, with variable absorption in shock. Cortisol testing fell away: CORTICUS showed the test didn't predict benefit, and ADRENAL and APROCCHSS enrolled on vasopressor need alone.

Source: Screenshot

pages.title: PRORATA and ProCAT trials showed little benefit from procalcitonin-guided antibiotics
pages.html: ProCAT (2018) found no difference in antibiotic days or adverse outcomes. PRORATA (2010) was done in settings with long courses at ward-level care.

pages.title: Set ventilator RR to match minute ventilation needs; in ARDS, titrate RR to pH (permissive hypercapnia), max ~35/min
pages.html:
No spontaneous breathing: set RR to achieve estimated pre-intubation minute ventilation (max ~35/min). Patient triggering every breath: set machine RR slightly below spontaneous RR, check ABG after ~30 min and adjust to PaCO2/pH. ARDS: pH 7.30–7.45 no change; 7.15–7.30 increase RR; <7.15 increase RR up to 35/min; persistent pH <7.15 consider cautiously increasing VT. Adjust RR to ABG and clinical condition.

Source: Screenshot

pages.title: Decompensated HF: check spot urine sodium at 2h and urine output at 6h, escalate loop diuretic if inadequate
pages.html:
IV furosemide 40 mg if loop-naive, or twice the usual oral dose IV if already on a loop. At 2h, urine Na <70 mmol/L: double the IV dose. At 6h, urine output <100 mL/h: double again. Ceiling furosemide 600 mg/day, up to 1,000 mg in severe renal impairment. PUSH-AHF: Na-guided escalation raised natriuresis (409 vs 345 mmol) but no difference in death or HF readmission at 180 days. 2026 ESC: class IIb.

Source: Screenshot

pages.title: Start CRRT in ventilated or vasopressor-dependent patients needing RRT
pages.html:
IHD had higher 90-day mortality in ICRAKI; CRRT looks the safer initial modality in unstable patients.

pages.title: Consider SC furosemide pump for HF patients needing ongoing parenteral diuretics
pages.html:
Allows early discharge with home decongestion instead of prolonged IV inpatient stay.

pages.title: Procalcitonin helps mainly where antibiotic courses are longer than guidance
pages.html: Most studies were in adult critical care. Benefit was seen only in settings using lots of antibiotics, where duration exceeded usual guidance.

pages.title: Avoid biopsying bony metastases where possible: decalcification prevents genetic testing
pages.html:
Bone samples are decalcified for analysis, which means genetic testing cannot be done on them. Choose a soft tissue site if available.

Source: SHM 2026

pages.title: No single best RRT mode: choose by haemodynamics, ICP, logistics and centre experience
pages.html:
IHD: 3-4 h, high blood/dialysate flow, fast solute and fluid shifts. SLED/PIRRT: 6-12 h, low efficiency, runs on an IHD machine, gentler than IHD. CRRT (SCUF, CVVH, CVVHD, CVVHDF): 24 h, slow and steady, best haemodynamics. PD: peritoneum as membrane, dialysate dwell and drain, no vascular access needed. Continuous and intermittent therapies are complementary.

Source: Screenshot

pages.title: RCC: metastasectomy is an option
pages.html:
Rarely, resection of a solitary metastasis is curative-intent in renal cell carcinoma.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Recurrent tiny pseudoaneurysms: segmental arterial mediolysis
pages.html:
Non-inflammatory arteriopathy giving a string-of-beads appearance; a vasculitis mimic.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Reverse halo (atoll) sign
pages.html:
Classic for cryptogenic organising pneumonia; also seen in mucormycosis and pulmonary infarction.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Low albumin hides a raised anion gap: add ~2.5 mEq/L per 1 g/dL below 4
pages.html:
Albumin is the largest unmeasured anion, so hypoalbuminaemia masks lactic acidosis and ketoacidosis behind a normal-looking gap (measured 12 at albumin 2 g/dL corrects to 17). Low albumin also raises the free fraction, so total phenytoin and calcium mislead: measure free phenytoin or ionised calcium rather than infusing albumin to normalise the total. Mechanism is not indication: trials raising albumin to a target in sepsis and cirrhosis (ALBIOS, ARISS, ATTIRE) did not improve survival.

Source: Screenshot

pages.title: Use the lowest FiO2 that gives adequate oxygenation; in ARDS target SpO2 88–95%
pages.html:
Aim for the lowest FiO2 that achieves adequate oxygenation. In ARDS, the lung-protective SpO2 target is 88–95%. Avoid unnecessarily prolonged exposure to high FiO2, as hyperoxia can harm the lungs.

Source: Screenshot

pages.title: In haemodynamically unstable or raised-ICP patients, choose CRRT over intermittent HD (KDIGO)
pages.html:
IHD (3-4 h, 300-400 mL/min) causes fast UF, more hypotension and disequilibrium risk. SLED (6-12 h) is intermediate. CRRT (24 h, 100-250 mL/min) is slow and steady, best tolerated haemodynamically, with the lowest ICP risk, but needs anticoagulation for filter life. KDIGO suggests CRRT over standard intermittent RRT in haemodynamically unstable patients and in acute brain injury, raised ICP or cerebral oedema. Solute removal is by diffusion in IHD and SLED, and by convection, diffusion or both in CRRT.

Source: Screenshot

pages.title: Arrange clinical review every 3 days for home SC diuretic patients
pages.html:
Trial protocol reviewed patients every 3 days while on treatment.

Trial: SUBCUT-HF II

pages.title: SCAI classification of cardiogenic shock
pages.html:
Stages A (at risk) → B (beginning) → C (classic) → D (deteriorating) → E (extremis).

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Serum ACE is not useful in sarcoidosis
pages.html:
Normal in 20–50% of cases, and does not track disease activity or treatment response.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Prefer volume-controlled ventilation in ARDS: it gives reliable control of tidal volume for lung protection
pages.html:
Volume-controlled ventilation (standard VC or PRVC) allows reliable control of VT, which is particularly useful when lung-protective ventilation is required. In pressure control, a set inspiratory pressure is delivered, so VT varies with lung compliance and resistance.

Source: Screenshot

pages.title: Splenic or portal vein thrombosis: think myeloproliferative neoplasm
pages.html:
Unexplained splanchnic vein thrombosis should prompt a JAK2 check — MPN (especially PV/ET) is a classic hidden cause.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Spot urine sodium predicts loop diuretic response
pages.html:
Check urine sodium 1–2 h after the dose: >90–100 mmol/L = good natriuretic response; <70 = poor response, escalate.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Scabies: delta-wing sign on dermoscopy plus mites/eggs on scraping confirm diagnosis
pages.html:
Intense generalised itch, worse at night, with affected household contacts. Papules and excoriations in finger webs, wrists and axillae. Dermoscopy: delta-wing sign at end of short serpiginous burrow; scraping shows mites and eggs.

Source: Screenshot

pages.title: Avoid routine CVP/ScvO2 targets
pages.html:
Don't use CVP or ScvO2 targets routinely; individualise resuscitation.

pages.html:
Variant of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease: Thrombocytopenia, Anasarca, Fever, Reticulin fibrosis, Organomegaly. From Clinical Problem Solvers.

pages.html:
Still measure it; look for the delta. Use sex-specific cut-offs.

pages.html:

pages.title: Type 1 MI includes SCAD
pages.html:
Spontaneous coronary artery dissection is a type 1 MI; expect a dynamic troponin rise in the hundreds.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Type 2 MI needs proof — otherwise it's acute myocardial injury
pages.html:
4th/5th Universal Definition: ischaemic injury ≠ type 2 MI. To limit overdiagnosis, type 2 MI requires imaging evidence (new RWMA, newly non-viable myocardium) or confirmed obstructive CAD. An acute troponin rise not meeting criteria = acute myocardial injury.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Varenicline for smoking cessation
pages.html:
Possibly under-used; worth offering more often.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Ultrasound guidance improves radial arterial line success compared with palpation
pages.html:
Reel from @zentensivist on improving radial arterial catheter lifespan, citing two meta-analyses of RCTs (Am Heart J 2018; Indian J Anaesth 2025) comparing ultrasound-guided and palpation-guided radial artery catheterisation. Screenshot gives no figures, so check the papers for first-pass success and complication data.

pages.title: Morphine suits end-of-life care and air hunger but needs caution in kidney disease
pages.html: 1-10 mg/hr. It can cause hypotension, and renal metabolism means it accumulates in kidney disease.

pages.title: Epinephrine: beta effects at low dose, alpha at high dose; consider in bradycardia
pages.html: It increases cardiac output, so it suits patients who are on the bradycardic side.

pages.title: Wellens' pattern = critical proximal LAD stenosis
pages.html:
Biphasic or deeply inverted T waves in V2–V3 while pain-free; needs angiography, not a stress test.

Source: Teaching notes 16/09/2026 (Conan Liu)

pages.title: Eosinophilia is mild in adrenal insufficiency; marked eosinophilia points to parasites or malignancy
pages.html:
Drugs and adrenal insufficiency cause only mild eosinophil elevation. Parasitic infection and malignancy cause severe elevation. Use the degree of eosinophilia to guide the differential.

Source: Screenshot

pages.title: Give dexamethasone
pages.html:
RECOVERY (2020): Dexamethasone reduced 28-day mortality in ventilated/oxygen-requiring patients, not in those without oxygen. Hydroxychloroquine, lopinavir-ritonavir, azithromycin and convalescent plasma showed no benefit.

Trial: RECOVERY

Source: RECOVERY

pages.title: Steroids raise the white cell count, peaking around 48 hours
pages.html:
Steroid-induced neutrophilia is dose-related: with prednisolone 40–60 mg the rise is generally higher, with peak WCC at about 48 hours. The figure '~4.8' in the original note is unclear; check it.

Source: quick

pages.title: Bicarbonate in acidosis: benefit is unproven, with any signal confined to AKI subgroups and reduced RRT use
pages.html:
Metabolic acidosis (pH <7.30) impairs myocardial contractility and causes vasodilation and vasopressor resistance, leading to hypoperfusion, AKI and multiorgan failure. BICAR-ICU showed no difference in the primary outcome, with a mortality benefit only in the moderate-severe AKI subgroup, plus reduced RRT use. BICAR-ICU 2 showed no mortality benefit in moderate-severe AKI but reduced RRT use. Earlier trials focused on severe acidosis (pH <7.20) or AKI cohorts, whereas SODa-BIC targets mild-moderate acidosis in shock.

Source: Screenshot

pages.title: Individualise MAP target
pages.html:
Reassess individually; chronic hypertension may raise the autoregulation floor.

pages.title: Hydromorphone for opioid-resistant patients; caution in liver disease
pages.html: 0.2-3 mg/hr. Can cause some hypotension compared with fentanyl and is hepatically metabolised so may accumulate. Switching from fentanyl can avoid the context-sensitive half-life problem.
